questions.q: What does Casey Lindqvist actually ask for in this lesson?
options: To remove the autoscaler entirely
To pin node pool and HPA capacity with real headroom, instead of relying on the autoscaler's reaction time during the next sale
To reduce the number of availability zones in use
To cancel the next sale
questions.explain: Casey's position is that fixed, pinned headroom is simpler and safer than depending on the autoscaler to react fast enough again.

questions.q: What is Dana Whitfield's core objection to pinning capacity high across the board?
options: She doesn't believe the incident actually happened
It would recreate, permanently, the exact over-provisioning cost problem that autoscaling exists to prevent
She thinks Engineering should have no say in capacity at all
She wants to switch cloud providers entirely
questions.explain: Dana's FinOps-grounded point is that fixed capacity sized for peak pays for that peak many times over on every day it isn't actually needed.

questions.q: Why is 'pin it high' specifically NOT a fix for what actually caused the original incident?
options: Because the incident was caused by an uneven distribution of capacity across availability zones, not by too little total capacity
Because the incident was unrelated to capacity in any way
Because Casey's proposal would use the wrong cloud provider
Because more capacity always makes distribution problems worse automatically
questions.explain: More capacity distributed the same unsafe way doesn't obviously fix a distribution problem — the root cause Lessons 12-13 diagnosed and fixed.

questions.q: Why does 'just split the difference' between Casey's and Dana's numbers fail as a resolution?
options: Because it's against company policy
Because neither side's number is based on a real measurement yet, so averaging two guesses just produces a different guess that satisfies neither concern
Because Casey and Dana would never agree to compromise
Because it's technically impossible to average two replica counts
questions.explain: Averaging unmeasured guesses doesn't produce a correct number — it just hides the fact that no one has looked at real data yet.

questions.q: What specific piece of information is identified as missing from this conversation, and already available?
options: A new hire to mediate the dispute
The real, measured per-AZ peak-load data captured by the FinOps dashboard's per-AZ panel during the actual sale
A vendor quote for additional cloud spend
A survey of customer satisfaction
questions.explain: The real sale already produced exactly the data needed to settle this with evidence instead of instinct — it just hasn't been pulled into the room yet.
